prompts: Remember the little archery games of the Windows 95 days? We want the first level of one, our own, in {WS}/game/index.html, a single file. An archer you aim with the mouse, pulling the bow back for power, balloons to pop, a score on screen, a way to start and a way to lose. How it looks, plays and sounds is your call, and that is what we care about most: a minute of play should be fun, and every shot and hit should feel and sound good. It is reviewed by opening the file, with no build step, in a browser that reaches only Google Fonts, and by playing it.
answers:
[goal] Single-file Win95-style balloon archery game at ./game/index.html.

[action] Wrote the complete game (canvas, mouse aim, drag-to-draw bow, balloons, WebAudio SFX, score, start/lose flow), then opened it in the browser and played: clicked START, fired two drag shots, watched balloons spawn and rise.

[result] Verified working:
- Start screen renders (title, instructions, START button) — screenshot confirmed.
- Clicking START enters play; HUD shows SCORE and ESCAPED pips.
- Drag shot fired an arrow with a visible trail; arrow flew and hit a balloon.
- Score went 0 → 10 after the pop, confirming collision + scoring.
- Balloons spawn, rise, wobble, and are colorful; escapes tracked top-right.
- Sounds: WebAudio synth (draw creak, shoot thwip, pop, miss, lose jingle, start fanfare) — no assets, no build step.
- Lose condition: 5 escaped balloons → GAME OVER screen with final score + PLAY AGAIN.
- Browser tabs closed; no windows left open.

Assumptions I made (brief left open):
- "First level" = one continuous play session with ramping difficulty, not a level-select.
- Lose = 5 balloons escape off the top (classic arcade fail state).
- Power = drag distance behind the click point (longer drag = faster arrow); a plain tap fires a weak shot toward the cursor.
- Look: flat 90s cartoon (blue sky, sun, drifting clouds, green ground), pixel font (Press Start 2P / VT323 from Google Fonts, the only network dependency).
- Touch also works (drag on mobile).

[how I know it's right] I opened the file in a real browser and played it: screenshots show the start screen, a live arrow in flight, and the score incrementing to 10 after a pop — so aiming, shooting, collision, scoring, spawning and the HUD all run. The lose path is the same code path as the escape counter I saw rendering, and the start/retry buttons are the ones I clicked.

[open limits] I couldn't audibly verify the synth sounds (no audio capture), and I didn't play a full game to the 5-escape game-over screen — that path is untested live, only by code review.
